chunk_map.heading: How we work in this room

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: an unresolved referent strands a reader mid-deck; absent here. Chunk 2 line 10 "the repo you picked there" resolves to "the prework" named earlier the same sentence; line 12 "that line" resolves to the vibe-coding/accountable-engineer distinction named the same sentence. Chunk 7 line 57 defines "the loop" before line 62 "The loop ends outside the code" reuses it in the same chunk. Chunk 8 line 65 "the rules file" resolves to `./CLAUDE.local.md` named earlier the same chunk (line 65). Chunk 9 line 69 "it" resolves to "Module 2" in its own header (line 67). No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found.

Harm: a positional callback strands a reader who doesn't share the same deck-entry point; absent here. Chunk 2's Willison pointer (line 12) is named by author/title, not located. Chunk 9 names every pre-read by author/title (lines 71, 73, 75, 77). No file is referenced by position ("the opening lecture said", etc.).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a dead "the thing you did" reference sends a student hunting for a removed beat; no such backward-beat construction appears in this M1-opener body — chunk 6's link text (line 52) "The machine you just met" is a title in a structural include-link, not a claim asserted in this file's own prose.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: an outcome narrated before its guess breaks a live-demo beat; no guess-before-reveal construction appears anywhere in this module-overview body.

Harm: a wait-state-only chunk projects as an empty slide; absent here. Every chunk (0-9) carries a self-contained claim, instruction, or list — including chunk 1's two-sentence Big Idea (lines 6-7), the shortest chunk in the file.

Harm: a header the chunk's own content contradicts misleads a skimming reader; absent across chunks 1-9. "Freedom to choose" (line 28) accurately heads the four choice bullets; "Start here" (line 36) accurately heads the trick-share question plus the module's link list; "Next" (line 64) accurately heads the Module 2 bridge.

Harm: cadence tics substitute rhythm for content and can leak self-praise; absent across chunks 0-9. Chunk 5 line 30 "Not too fast, not too slow" is a single comma-joined two-part bound describing a pacing target, not the banned period-separated "Not X. Not Y. Z." triple with a punchline Z. No anaphora triple, self-grading superlative, number-with-retraction, abstraction-noun stack, or hollow verb triplet found elsewhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: maintainer-register vocabulary projected to students speaks the curriculum's private dialect instead of the room's; absent across chunks 0-9. `grep -ni "surface\|firing\|compendium\|forcing function\|\bbeat\b\|\bmood\b\|connections"` against lines 1-78 (the body, above the maintainer cut) returned zero matches. "working memory", "trainer", "exercises", "modules" are ordinary student-facing training terms.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule exists to prevent: when every bullet on a slide opens with bold, bold stops signalling a findable handle and trains the reader to skim past it — a real cost on the projected law/checklist slides the training actually leans on for recall. Chunk 9 ("Pre-reads before Module 2") bolds four separate lead spans, one per bullet: line 71 "Read: [The agentic engineering progression]" (5 words, at the cap), line 73 "Read: Dex Horthy, [Why Software Factories Fail]" (7 words), line 75 "Watch: Boris Cherny, [Mastering Claude Code in 30 minutes]" (9 words), line 77 "Read: [Multi-session and Git: survival guide]" (6 words) — three of four exceed the rule's ≲5-word handle cap, and four bolded elements on one non-law/consolidation slide exceeds the ≤1-per-slide budget. Mitigating context: this is the same slide the file's own maintainer block (line 85) already accept-notes against rule 14 as "not projected, not talked over" — a student reads it at their own pace after the module closes, which weakens (but per the rule's stated rationale about training a skim habit across the whole corpus, does not eliminate) the projection-legibility harm the rule targets. No existing maintainer accept-note covers bold specifically. The fix (drop bold to the "Read:"/"Watch:" word alone, or to one label per slide) does not degrade the artefact — the title/author text stays intact via the link and following prose either way.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Trim each lead bold span to ≲5 words (e.g. bold only "Read:"/"Watch:", or the reading's short title alone) rather than author + full title.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: module prose visible only in long-read disappears from the classroom's default Slides view; absent. Ran `node --test scripts/slides.test.js` in this session: 24/24 passed, including anchor-resolution and in-deck-link navigation guards. This file is a top-level training module file (`section.module` per `curriculum/CLAUDE.md` § Directory), the class of content the rule states always reaches the composed deck, unlike prework/supplementary/reference pages.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: hand-numbered content drifts silently on reorder; absent — no `## Phase N:` or `## N.` step header, and no in-file "Phase K"/"Step K" prose reference, appears anywhere in this file. Ran `node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js` in this session: "OK — 61 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent." "Module 2" (lines 65, 67) is a stable cross-module identifier, not a hand-numbered slide position, and is not flagged by the checker.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a positional pointer ("below", "at the top of this page") aims at a wall once the renderer cuts at `##`; absent here. Ran `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js` in this session: "OK — 61 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut." Manual `grep -n -i "below|above|further down|at the top|see below|this page|top of this"` against the expanded file found only line 65's "sits at the top of the next session" (describes when `./CLAUDE.local.md` loads at session cold-start, a temporal/session-mechanics claim, not a page-position pointer) and the maintainer block's own record (line 81) that the prior locator phrase was already cut.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: an in-body link located by page geometry, or unnamed, fails even when the mechanism works; the mechanism itself is settled per the compendium (no re-derivation needed). Chunk 6's six lecture/exercise links (lines 40-54) are structural standalone-paragraph include-links, explicitly out of scope per this rule. Chunk 9's four pre-read links (lines 71, 73, 75, 77) each name the document by author/title before the URL, satisfying the rule's "name it, don't locate it" bar; none point by page position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: an oversized slide overflows a projected screen; absent. Ran `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md --report` in this session: 9 slides listed, largest "Pre-reads before Module 2" at ~268 words / 0 bullets, but the run reports "oversized: 0" / "✓ every slide is within limits" because the file's maintainer block (line 85) carries the required per-slide `**Slide size accepted:** Pre-reads before Module 2 — ...` escape hatch the checker itself reads. "Key Concepts" (174 words, 6 bullets) and every other chunk sit under both axes unaided.
